page_title: KNXBench — Your KNX project. Your workbench.
description: Import KNX projects, edit your installation and see what the bus is saying. Meet KNXBench: an independent engineering app, in your browser via Docker or natively on Linux.
preview_note: Local design preview · Not published yet
hero_lede: Import projects. Work with devices and group addresses. See what the bus is saying. KNXBench brings your installation into a modern engineering workspace.
platforms: In your browser via Docker. Or natively on Linux.
hero_alt: The real KNXBench app in the dark Graphite theme: group addresses from a fictional sample house and the kitchen light inspector.
strip_three: Project data with clear import reports
features_title:
From a project file
to a clear picture.
features_intro: You know your installation. Your tools should help you understand it, not get in the way.
feature_one_body: Import supported ETS projects with a report of warnings and limitations. Continue in KNXBench’s own versioned format. Or start a new project from scratch.
feature_two_body: Topology, buildings, devices, group addresses and links in one workbench. With search, an inspector and undo/redo, so the next change stays understandable too.
feature_three_body: Observe telegrams over KNXnet/IP, inspect values and explore communication as a table or flow view. Individual messages become a picture you can follow.
watch_title:
Don’t just read about it.
See it.
watch_intro: Short looks at the real application. Every recording uses fictional sample data, not somebody’s actual installation.
project_body: Add a device from the product catalog, assign a free address and link a communication object to a group address. Without jumping between five different tools.
project_transcript: A push button is selected, named and created with a free individual address in the sample house. Its first communication object is then linked to 0/0/2 “Kitchen light”. The recording uses zoom and time compression; it is not a real-time performance test.
project_caption: Real app · Sample house · Recording with zoom and time compression
flow_body: The flow view brings senders, receivers and values together. Here it shows lights, blinds and temperature in the sample house, using synthetic telegrams and an optional CRT theme.
flow_transcript: Synthetic telegrams make devices appear in the flow view: lights turn on and off, a blind goes down, and temperature and valve values change. The recording shows the real monitor component; no live bus is connected.
flow_caption: Real monitor component · Synthetic traffic · No live bus
details_body: Filter group addresses, select an address and inspect its properties right beside it. A calm workspace for the details that matter.
details_transcript: The real app shows 15 group addresses from a fictional sample house. Filtering for “Kitchen” narrows the table; 0/0/2 is selected and its properties appear in the inspector. The filter is then cleared. API answers are offline demo data; no live server or bus is operated.
details_caption: Real app · Offline demo data · No hardware contact
video_fallback: Your browser cannot play this video.
personality_body: There are calm interfaces for focused work. And, when you feel like it, green phosphor and a small starship bridge. Themes, language packs and optional achievements add a little personality.
crt_alt: The real group address table in the optional green CRT theme with fictional sample data.
crt_caption: A little phosphor on your workbench.
lcars_alt: The real KNXBench workbench in the optional LCARS theme with fictional sample data.
optional_themes: Optional. The underlying workbench stays the same. Screenshots: real app with offline demo data.
story_title:
How an idea
became a workbench.
story_body: It began with wanting a KNX tool on Linux. Then came decisions, detours, AI assistants and rather a lot of “just one more thing”. The Evolution Story follows that path, with evidence and a slightly melancholy narrator.
status_title:
Already a workbench.
Still an alpha.
status_body: KNXBench is under active development. Try it, keep backups and check whether your project and devices fit the supported scope. Your feedback helps make the next version better.
status_summary: Project work, product data and bus diagnostics are at the core. Import support and device operations have explicitly documented boundaries: not every format or device has the same level of support.
scope_import: ETS project import is limited to supported formats and versions. Warnings and unsupported content are surfaced in the import report; full ETS compatibility is not promised.
scope_export: After import, you work in .knxdb. Export back to .knxproj is not provided.
scope_hardware: Commissioning and device downloads support limited, documented paths. Project editing does not mean every device can be programmed.
scope_secure: KNX Secure is not currently implemented.
backup_note: Try a copy first. Read the application’s guidance before hardware operations.
demos_title:
A project to explore.
No installation to risk.
demos_intro: Three fictional offline projects for your own KNXBench instance. Each ZIP includes a native .knxdb, the shared fictional product catalogue and an English tour with five exercises.
demos_home_summary: 32 devices, 105 group addresses. Two living floors, basement and outside areas.
demos_residential_summary: 101 devices, 339 group addresses. Six apartments, three living floors and shared areas.
demos_office_summary: 157 devices, 507 group addresses. Three floors with offices, meeting rooms and auxiliary areas.
demos_all: Download all three demos (ZIP on GitHub)
demos_setup: Extract a ZIP and keep an untouched reset copy. Install fictional-demo-devices.knxprod once through Product catalog, then open a copy of the .knxdb via File → Open. Native edits can auto-save.
demos_safety: Offline exploration only. Fictional applications contain no firmware and must never be downloaded to real devices. These projects are not ETS exports or electrical plans.
demos_version_note: Demo version 1.0.0. The frozen ZIP READMEs retain their original “local review candidate” label. See the guide for the tested development build; compatibility with older alpha releases is not promised.
start_title:
The next view
is your own.
start_body: No account with us. No hosted demo. KNXBench runs on your own instance, so you try the real product.
launch_note: The repository and its alpha downloads are public on GitHub. This website itself is still a preview and not published yet.
docker_body: Use the web app through a suitable Docker environment on your system. The container brings the interface and server together; you stay in control of your projects.
docker_step_two: Build the image, configure persistent storage and access.
docker_step_three: Open it in your browser, create a project or import a copy.
docker_note: Live bus communication has additional networking requirements. Docker is not a promise of identical hardware connectivity on every host system.
native_body: The AppImage packages the desktop application for Linux. Find system requirements, alpha version information and installation guidance with the releases.
native_note: Choose an alpha version, read the release notes and work with project copies.
support_intro: You don’t have to figure it all out alone.
footer_tagline: An independent workbench for KNX projects.
independence: KNXBench is an independent project. It is not affiliated with the KNX Association and is not KNX certified. KNX and ETS are mentioned to describe the application’s scope.
license_note: Free software under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Free to use, including commercially, subject to the licence terms.
privacy_body: This website uses no analytics scripts, marketing cookies, embedded video services or remotely hosted fonts. Media and fonts load from the same site host. GitHub links lead to an external service.
privacy_pending: Before public launch, information about the actual hosting, possible server logs and privacy enquiries will be added and reviewed. This local preview is not a final privacy notice for the future site.
contact_body: Public project feedback and support gaps can be reported on GitHub in the KNXBench repository, using its support-gap form. Share only information explicitly approved for public disclosure, not confidential projects or credentials.
privacy_hosting: This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. According to GitHub's documentation, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored for security purposes when a GitHub Pages site is visited. For privacy enquiries, use the contact on the legal notice page.
